footprint.notes: State rows are FDIC Summary of Deposits data (regulator tier) for Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. only (cert 3511), as of June 30, 2026, the newest survey (FY2026, after the FY2025 fiscal year the records use); the per-state office counts and deposit sums are the FDIC API's own aggregation (agg_by=STALPBR), whose counts total 4,157, matching the API's record total. The FDIC reports deposits in $ thousands; they are stored in $ millions (divided by 1,000, three decimals kept, no rounding). Two single-office Wells Fargo banks are excluded and not added in: Wells Fargo Bank South Central, N.A. (cert 5146, Houston TX, $1,673,209 thousand) and Wells Fargo National Bank West (cert 27389, Las Vegas NV, $6,933,675 thousand). The zero-deposit rows (MA, MI, MO) are single trust offices (service type 30: Boston, Birmingham MI, Saint Louis). Country rows and sites are occupied square footage from the FY2025 10-K Item 2 table of top U.S. and international locations (Dec 31, 2025; unit 'square-feet-millions'); 'All other international locations' (0.3) and 'All other U.S. locations' (26.6) are not mapped. San Antonio-New Braunfels, TX dropped out of the 10-K's top U.S. locations in FY2025 and its site was replaced by the newly listed Philadelphia-Camden-Wilmington metro area. The 10-K also says ~76% of ~205,000 active employees are U.S.-based; no state or country employee split is published there. No company-published state impact report was used.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025 Form 10-K, accession 0000072971-26-000133; financial statements in wfc-20251231.htm). Bank: paidOut null, altPaidOut = noninterest expense − D&A − SBC + income taxes paid. Operating cash flow was negative (−19,001), driven by trading and loans-held-for-sale flows, which is why the formula is not used. D&A is premises-and-equipment depreciation (1.7bn as stated in the accounting-policy note, the DepreciationAndAmortization fact); the cash-flow add-back 'Depreciation, amortization and accretion' includes securities and loan accretion and is not comparable, so it is not used. SBC is the stock-based compensation credited to paid-in capital (1,476, the ShareBasedCompensation fact). The cash-flow statement has no premises-and-equipment purchase line, so capex is null. Interest paid (39,806) is shown separately.
